messages.author: 39d1746e02aeb249
messages.subject: Specifying time window periods when running GGIR
parts:
Hi all, 

Could I check with you regarding time window periods. 

From what I understand, if we want to run GGIR during specific time window periods instead of the usual 0-24, I would need to change these 2 variables: 
 
qwindow = c(7,18) (previously 0,24)
includedaycrit= 10 (previously 16)

Based on the outputs that we get, we see that the values are very similar for the same subject. Is this normal? 

Or do we also have to specify/change another variable in the ggir code?

Thanks! 

Regards, 
Claire

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Specifying time window periods when running GGIR
parts:
​Correct.

includedaycrit= 10 (previously 16)

I am not this is what you want. It means that days with up to 14 of invalid data can be included, which means that up to 14 hours of data are imputed. If multiple days in the recording have high levels of accelerometer non-wear then those days will have similar levels of physical activity because of the imputation as the imputation is the same for all days.

So, I think it is best to motivate includedaycrit only based on the wear instruction given to the participants. If it is a 24/7 wear instruction then going below 16 hours would not be advisable.

Thanks,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

​

In the package vignettes https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/index.html you will find an overview of all the functionality GGIR offers including a discussion of output variables. A good starting point may be https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html 

If you are still not sure how to interpret the GGIR output then consider booking a GGIR training course: https://www.accelting.com/ggir-training/ We still have some seats left for the standard training in November.

Regards,
Vincent
